transcript:
>> This is "NPR News Now," the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from "NPR News" in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton.
President Trump says Alaska Democratic Senate candidate
Mary Peltola should suffer, quote,
"legal and political consequences."
It comes after "The New York Times" published a story
that said her campaign recruited a candidate
with the same name as her Republican opponent.
The report relies on text messages showing Peltola's
campaign coordinated with operatives
to recruit a retired schoolteacher named Dan J. Sullivan
to run for the seat currently held
by Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan.
Democrats in the Peltola campaign have denied
they had anything to do with his candidacy.
With less than a week to go until Election Day,
President Trump is campaigning in Ohio,
Vice President J.D. Vance is in North Carolina,
and as NPR's Stephen Fowler reports,
former President Barack Obama is rallying
with Democrats in Atlanta.
>> In state and federal races across the country,
the Democratic pitch to voters focuses on a few things,
like tackling affordability issues,
like rising gas prices and high inflation,
fighting corruption, protecting healthcare access,
and perhaps, most importantly, not being Republicans.
After the Democratic Party lost control
of the White House and Congress in 2024,
polls show voters have grown dissatisfied
with President Trump and Republican leadership, too.
That's one reason both parties are spending
hundreds of millions of dollars in the final weeks
on a relatively small number of races
that could decide who controls the House and Senate,
and governors' races, like the one in Georgia,
where former President Obama is campaigning.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Atlanta.
>> A new report finds that a federal immigration program
that deputizes local police for enforcement work
is now responsible for a big share of immigration arrests,
and Piers Jaclyn Diaz has the story.
>> The Department of Homeland Security has said
that its 287(g) program is a critical tool
to cut down on crime.
That program gives power to state and local police
to help in immigration enforcement.
And the 287(g) task force agreement
allows police to make immigration arrests.
Under President Trump's second term,
participation in the program has dramatically expanded.
That's according to a new report
from the immigration reform advocacy group Forward.US.
They found that more than 29,000 officers
were deputized by ICE between January 2025
and October of this year.
That's far more than the 11,600 deportation officers
employed by ICE directly.
Forward says we can expect to see the program continue to grow.
Jaclyn Diaz, NPR News.
>> The Federal Reserve chose not to raise interest rates
as inflation remains stubborn.
The Fed opted to stand pat after raising rates
at its last policy meeting for the first time
in more than three years,
saying more time is needed to assess the results.
The Fed is now widely expected to raise interest rates
at its next policy meeting in December,
two policymakers dissented voting instead
to raise them by a quarter percentage point.
U.S. stocks ticked higher today.
The S&P 500 rose about a quarter percent.
This is NPR News.
During the peak of the 2025 L.A. fires,
about seven million residents
were exposed to airborne lead concentrations
that exceeded 80 times the normal background level.
That's according to a study in the journal Science Advances.
Researchers found that the urban smoke had lead, arsenic,
and other toxic metals linked to burning vehicles,
building materials, and electronics.
A growing number of adults are buying toys
and engaging in playful activities,
according to a recent Harris Poll.
As NPR's Katherine Welch reports,
millennials and Gen Z led the spending.
>> A recent Harris Poll surveyed a little more
than 2,000 Americans, 18 and older,
about how toys and play factor into their lives.
Think board games and video games,
coloring books, and theme parks.
>> The survey found that this play, known as cudolting,
beat out therapy, drinking, and parties
as preferred ways to unwind.
Nearly half said they felt judged for playing,
but that didn't stop them.
The U.S. toy market is about $46 billion,
according to the Toy Association.
And the survey says millennials and Gen Z
are the largest adult group spending money to play.
Nostalgia is what's pushing their emotional buttons.
Respondents say they connect with brands
from their childhood.
They also want games created for adults,
but those are harder to come by.
Katherine Welch, NPR News.
>> South Africa says it has sent
the world's longest freight train on a test run.
It's 4.7 miles long with 696 wagons,
which were empty for the two-day journey
from a port to an iron ore mine,
and then in the interior of the country.
This is NPR.

topics.text: President Trump says Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola should face legal and political consequences
Report says Peltola campaign recruited a same-named candidate, Dan J. Sullivan, to run against Republican Dan S. Sullivan
Trump campaigns in Ohio, Vance in North Carolina, and Obama rallies Democrats in Atlanta ahead of midterms
Democrats campaign on affordability, corruption, and healthcare as midterm races draw heavy spending
New report finds 287(g) program deputizing local police now accounts for large share of immigration arrests
Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as inflation remains stubborn; December hike widely expected
Study finds about seven million Los Angeles residents exposed to elevated airborne lead during 2025 fires
Harris Poll finds adults, especially millennials and Gen Z, increasingly spending on toys and play
South Africa runs test of the world's longest freight train, 4.7 miles with 696 empty wagons
